philosophy: Give {cat_name} a boundary that is visibly, reliably theirs, so the nervous energy spent defending or watching an ambiguous one has somewhere to stand down. This works by adding certainty, not by removing stimulus.
typical_duration: 7-10 days of a nightly minimum-5-minute practice
contraindications: households with 3+ cats sharing the same main doorway — territorial routines can escalate friction between cats rather than settle it; pair this with the resource-generosity treatment instead
cats under 4 months old — territorial marking behavior isn't yet meaningful at this age

name_mystical: The Slow Return to the Room
philosophy: {cat_name}'s system isn't broken by company, it's flooded by too much of it too fast. This works by shrinking the dose of stimulation until it's tolerable, then lengthening it in controlled steps, rather than by forcing tolerance through repeated exposure.
material_categories: a designated safe room or space
typical_duration: 2-3 weeks of practice around any social gathering, with the first week focused on setup alone
contraindications: homes with frequent unscheduled visitors — a graded exposure plan can't work if the actual exposures stay unpredictable; anchor this to gatherings you can plan ahead of time
very small homes with no separable room — adapt using a covered crate or carrier as the safe space instead

name_mystical: The Rite of the Steady Threshold
philosophy: {cat_name}'s alarm isn't about the door, it's about what the door has come to predict. This works by decoupling the pre-departure cues from the departure itself, so the signal stops carrying the same charge.
typical_duration: 10-14 days, including several short practice departures that aren't real errands
contraindications: cats already working with a vet on separation anxiety — bring this ritual in as a companion practice alongside that care, not a replacement for it
households where departure cues can't be controlled (e.g. shared entryways with roommates on different schedules) — focus the ritual on the scent-item step alone

philosophy: {cat_name}'s system is built to predict, not to improvise. This works by giving the day a small number of genuinely fixed points, so the body can relax into the gaps between them instead of staying braced for the next unknown.
typical_duration: 2-3 weeks to establish, since circadian patterns shift slowly
contraindications: households with rotating shift work where no two days share the same schedule — anchor the ritual to the least-variable point in the day (usually the last feeding) rather than a fixed clock time
kittens under 6 months — their sleep cycles are naturally fragmented and shouldn't be treated as disordered

name_mystical: The Investiture of the Anchor Object
philosophy: {cat_name} has already found the mechanism that works — a fixed point to return to under stress. This works by formalizing and protecting that mechanism instead of second-guessing or removing it.
material_categories: a designated safe location for it
typical_duration: ongoing — this is a maintenance ritual, not a time-limited course of treatment
contraindications: if the anchor object could be swallowed or choked on (small parts, string, foam) — keep the ritual to a lookalike duplicate instead; the point is comfort, not risk
if the fixation intensified suddenly and recently — a vet visit belongs ahead of this ritual, in case there's more than habit going on

philosophy: Guarding behavior is a response to scarcity that's felt, even when it isn't real. This works by making resource abundance visible and spatially obvious, so there's nothing left to compete over.
material_categories: a resource map of the home
typical_duration: 1-2 weeks to redistribute resources, then ongoing maintenance
contraindications: single-cat households — this ritual is specifically for tension between cohabiting cats and won't apply
very small homes where physical separation of stations isn't possible — use visual barriers (furniture, room dividers) as a substitute for distance

philosophy: The voice isn't the problem, it's the request — usually for attention, food, or engagement that isn't reliably arriving on its own. This works by giving that request a predictable, quieter channel to travel through.
material_categories: a non-vocal request signal (e.g. a mat or bell)
typical_duration: 2-3 weeks — vocal habits that have been reinforced for a long time take longer to shift than they took to form
contraindications: sudden, out-of-character vocal escalation in an older cat — that's a vet-first situation, not a ritual-first one
multi-cat homes where the vocalizing cat may be responding to another cat's behavior — address any multi-cat tension first

name_mystical: The Release of the Held Voice
philosophy: {cat_name}'s stress is turning inward instead of outward — quiet instead of loud, groomed instead of expressed. This works by lowering ambient pressure and giving the body something safe to do with that energy besides self-directed grooming.
typical_duration: 2-3 weeks minimum, longer if grooming has caused visible coat or skin changes
contraindications: any visible skin damage, bald patches, or bleeding from grooming — that's past what any ritual is for; see a vet first, ritual second
recent major household change (move, new pet, new baby) — address stabilizing the environment first; this ritual works best once the underlying disruption has settled

philosophy: {cat_name}'s energy is looking for somewhere to go and is currently finding it in whatever's available — furniture, 3am sprints, shredded items. This works by giving that energy a structured, satisfying outlet before it finds an unstructured one.
typical_duration: 2 weeks to establish, then ongoing as a standing routine
contraindications: senior cats or cats with mobility limitations — favor low-impact foraging and puzzle enrichment over high-intensity chase play
cats already receiving significant daily play — if this diagnosis fired despite an already-active routine, focus on novelty (new objects/textures) rather than more volume of the same play

name_mystical: The Rite of the Ordinary Day
philosophy: No sharp imbalance stood out this time, and that itself is worth marking rather than skipping — {cat_name}'s current rhythm is worth reinforcing, not just leaving unattended until something breaks it.
material_categories: an existing favorite toy or object
typical_duration: ongoing, low-effort maintenance rather than a fixed course
contraindications: none specific — this is the general-maintenance path and has no household condition that redirects it elsewhere

philosophy: Give your cat space to recalibrate without pressure or fuss — the goal is patience, not intervention.
material_categories: a quiet resting spot near natural light
typical_duration: one sunbeam cycle
contraindications: Skip prompting or coaxing them toward the spot — let them find it unassisted.

philosophy: Clear the lingering hum with a calm, deliberate pass rather than more noise or activity.
material_categories: a lint roller or soft brush
typical_duration: 24 hours
contraindications: Skip if your cat is still startled by the vacuum — wait until they've fully settled first.

philosophy: Acknowledge the box as guarded territory and let your cat finish the ritual on their own terms.
typical_duration: one sitting
contraindications: Skip if your cat doesn't respond to catnip — offer a treat at the threshold instead.

philosophy: A small, announced change gives your cat something concrete to reorient around.
material_categories: the food bowl already in use
typical_duration: one evening
contraindications: Skip moving anything else in the room at the same time — one change at a time.

philosophy: Let the burst of energy run its course in a safe, lit space instead of trying to suppress it.
typical_duration: one night
contraindications: Skip if the zoomies routinely end in destructive behavior — that's a vet or behaviorist question, not a ritual one.

philosophy: Restore easy access to direct light — the disruption is about access, not the cat's mood.
typical_duration: the rest of the day
contraindications: Skip placing the cushion somewhere that blocks a walkway or door.

philosophy: A visible, repeated action signals the space is fully back under your cat's ownership.
typical_duration: one pass, once
contraindications: Skip if guests are still present — this works best once the room is empty again.

philosophy: A visible gesture of acknowledgment resolves the standoff faster than ignoring it does.
typical_duration: one gesture
contraindications: Skip if the corner hissing is new and persistent across many days — that's worth a vet visit, not just a ritual.

philosophy: A small, deliberate gesture at mealtime reframes the food as an offering rather than a routine chore.
typical_duration: one meal
contraindications: Skip if the pickiness lasts more than a couple of days — sustained appetite changes are a vet question.

philosophy: Respect the distance your cat is choosing rather than closing it for them.
material_categories: a low seat or floor cushion
typical_duration: five minutes, repeatable
contraindications: Skip making eye contact or reaching toward them — the point is that they approach, not you.
